item.title: Kamiarizuki: The Month the Gods Gather at Izumo — Guide
item.description: Across most of Japan, the tenth lunar month is called Kannazuki, ‘the month without gods’. In Izumo alone it is Kamiarizuki, ‘the month with gods’, because all eight million Shinto deities are believed to leave their home shrines and travel to Izumo Taisha to hold a great council — deciding, above all, the year’s en-musubi, the joining of human relationships and destinies. The festival is not a noisy public matsuri but a series of solemn rituals: the deities are ceremonially welcomed on the beach at night, housed in special halls during their stay, and formally seen off at the end.
